sections.heading: Clinic setup
sections.body:
A command-line batch importer reads manifests, validates resource names and writes one audit record per accepted item. Audit handles may be acquired inside a loop. A return from the validation helper can leave the handle open. An exception from append is caught by the caller and recorded as a skipped item. The starter kit includes a set of short functions in a language with explicit acquire and release operations; each resource is identified by an allocation site in this exercise.

For the first two functions, work entirely on paper. The third function is supplied as an AST in JSON and can be used for an optional implementation. Mark the entry, exit and exceptional exit separately. A node with no side effect still belongs in the graph if it controls reachability.

sections.heading: Written questions
sections.body: Draw a control-flow graph for the snippet under the stated exception model. Label the edge that leaves append on WriteError. Define a forward may analysis whose state at each program point is the set of sites whose handles can still be open. Give the transfer functions for acquisition, release and a branch join. Specify the entry fact and how you distinguish unreachable from reachable with the empty set. Show the facts after the first and second pass through the loop. Does one pass in source order yield the fixed point? Give a trace supporting your answer.

sections.heading: Metamorphic checks for the prototype
sections.body: Transform one function by introducing an equivalent conditional that uses a temporary variable and another by moving release into a cleanup block. The first transformation should preserve the reported leak sites. The second should remove an exceptional-exit report while retaining the intentional early-return finding unless that return also enters cleanup. Use at least one AST in which two acquisitions occur at distinct sites that happen to share a variable name. Include your assumptions about aliasing.

rows: Open site has no cleanup on that branch.
Earlier success does not close this handle.
Loop back edge must rejoin entry facts.

sections.heading: Submission
sections.body: For the core clinic, submit a labeled graph, the data-flow equations and the final fact sets for all exits. For the extension, include the JSON input, a runnable analysis and a regression test per transformation. The two tracks are separate. An answer describing how to test an analysis does not complete the implementation track. This document belongs to the program-analysis reading block and is separate from timed interview practice.
